Adding like fractions meaningfully requires understanding fractions as quantities or parts of a whole.
The rectangle and square formula calculates the area whose meaning is supplied by the general area concept.
Equivalent fractions must represent the same fractional quantity, for which the part-whole interpretation is foundational.
Equivalent fractions provide a direct common-denominator method, but fraction addition can be learned or performed by other methods.
The stated triangle-area formula requires identifying the base and its perpendicular height.
Recognising equivalent ratios requires understanding ratio notation and what the compared quantities represent.
Equivalent ratios help rescale ratios, but a quantity can be divided directly using unit parts and multiplication.
Interpreting expressions such as a+3 requires understanding that a letter denotes a number.
Fraction operations, especially with negative fractions, rely on the corresponding integer operations for signs and arithmetic.
The y=ax+b form supplies useful parameters for graphing, but linear graphs can also be constructed from tables or points.
Common-factor extraction gives useful experience with factoring and distributivity, but it is not required for factoring x²+px+q.
Prime factorisation requires identifying which factors are prime.
The dependent competence explicitly requires finding the HCF by prime factorisation.
The y=ax+b form supplies useful parameters for graphing, but linear graphs can also be constructed from tables or points.
Parallelogram area is a useful component formula for some composite figures, but composite figures need not contain parallelograms.
The y=ax+b form supplies useful parameters for graphing, but linear graphs can also be constructed from tables or points.
Quadratic factorisation is not required for the stated formula, completing-square, or graphical methods of solving the equations.
Side calculations reinforce interpreting trigonometric ratios, but inverse ratios for angles can be learned directly.
Exact special-angle values are values of the trigonometric functions, so the functions and their meanings are required.
Rate-of-change meaning helps interpret derivative notation, but the notation can be learned without prior conceptual mastery.
Standard notation is useful for stating differentiation results, but differentiating xⁿ does not depend on prior mastery of every notation convention.
Simplifying trigonometric expressions depends directly on applying identities relating the trigonometric functions.
Working with exponential and logarithmic functions and their graphs requires understanding what a function is.
The tangent-gradient interpretation motivates derivative formulae, but the formulae can be applied without that geometric interpretation.
Computing a normal probability from x₁, μ, and σ requires the standard-normal model and its standardisation role.
Using the mean and variance of a binomial distribution requires recognising the binomial model and its parameters.
Inverse functions depend on functions and on the associated domain and range of the mapping.
Rate-of-change meaning supports understanding differentiation, but standard-function derivative rules can be learned procedurally.
Computing a normal probability from x₁, μ, and σ requires the standard-normal model and its standardisation role.
A direct proof proceeds from a hypothesis to a conclusion, so conditional reasoning is its basic logical structure.
Existential quantifiers clarify existence claims, but an existence proof can be given by exhibiting a witness without formal quantifier notation.
De Moivre’s theorem for powers and roots is applied to complex numbers in polar or exponential form.
Partial derivatives require a function depending on multiple variables and the corresponding surface interpretation.
Solving first-order linear recurrences requires recurrence algebra, not prior analysis of sequence limits or general behaviour.
Analytic solutions provide examples for families of solution curves, but such families can be studied through slope fields or given solution forms.
